In the context of a hypothetical, write the jacket blurb for a thriller where a modern day operative of the FBI, ends up back in the early 1960's having to use her knowledge of "future" forensics to leave clues to enable her modern colleagues to catch a time-hopping serial-killer, before he dies.assistant
response:
"When FBI operative Rachel Jenkins is sent back in time to 1962, she finds herself in the midst of a decades-old serial killer case. The notorious 'Timekeeper' has been terrorizing the nation, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. As Rachel navigates the unfamiliar landscape of the past, she must use her knowledge of future forensic techniques to leave clues that will aid her modern colleagues in catching the killer.

With the help of a cryptic ally, Rachel sets out to unravel the Timekeeper's modus operandi, using her expertise in DNA analysis, fingerprinting, and ballistics to create a paper trail that will lead her team to the killer. But as she delves deeper into the case, Rachel realizes that the Timekeeper is not just a killer - he's a master of time itself.

As the body count rises, Rachel must use her wits and her knowledge of future forensic science to stay one step ahead of the Timekeeper. With the help of her colleagues, she must create a series of cryptic clues that will lead them to the killer before he strikes again. Can Rachel and her team catch the Timekeeper before he disappears into the timestream, or will he continue to leave a trail of bodies in his wake?

As the clock ticks down, Rachel must use all her skills and knowledge to outsmart the Timekeeper and bring him to justice. But as she looks around at the unfamiliar faces of the past, she realizes that she may be the only one who can see the truth. The Timekeeper's next victim is just 13 days away, and Rachel must act fast to prevent another murder. Can she solve the case before it's too late, or will the Timekeeper remain one step ahead?"
